benchmark_methodology.project_isolation_fix: v3 benchmark adds .claude-flow/ directory marker to force project-local memory.rvf and memory.pglite/. Without this, the CLI falls back to $HOME/.claude-flow/data/memory.rvf (user-global RVF) which accumulates state across runs and causes 'key already exists' errors when keys are reused. The committed baseline was captured under the broken behavior but happened to succeed because its bench-store-sqlite-* keys had no prior global collisions. Fix shipped in tests/benchmarks/adr0170-pglite-vs-sqlite.mjs (v1 → v2 schema bump).

cold_start.description: Fresh project dir; no prior .swarm/memory.pglite/; cli@latest first call pays pgvector cluster init + extension load + schema bootstrap + HNSW index create.

cold_init_indicators.interpretation: First-store at 1561ms vs steady-state ~955ms. ~600ms cold-init overhead on the very first call (pgvector cluster init + CREATE EXTENSION + per-controller CREATE TABLE/INDEX bootstrap). Amortized over 200 calls = 3ms/call.

warm_reopen.description: Same project dir as cold; .swarm/memory.pglite/ already populated; --key-suffix=warm ensures fresh keys (no upsert collisions).
warm_reopen.interpretation: Warm-reopen first-store is 998ms (vs cold's 1561ms — ~560ms saved on schema bootstrap idempotency). But subsequent calls are essentially flat with cold-start — every per-process CLI invocation pays its own substrate init cost. The 'warm' distinction matters only for the very first call after a process restart.

warmup_phase.interpretation: HNSW index build is amortized: cold first-10 mean is 1011ms, steady-state mean is 961ms — only ~50ms/call overhead in the warmup window. Cold-init outlier is exclusively on call #1.

comparison_vs_committed_baseline.baseline_capture_methodology: v1 schema; broken project-isolation (fell back to user-global $HOME/.claude-flow/data/memory.rvf). Stored to RVF only; never exercised the SQLite/Option F agentdb substrate at the memory_* axis. So this baseline measures the user-facing CLI memory store/search latency pre-pgvector, mostly dominated by CLI startup + embedding pipeline + RVF write.

comparison_vs_fresh_sqlite_v3.description: Fair apples-to-apples comparison: SQLite path (cli@patch.36 + agentdb@patch.48 with Option F sqlite-vec) re-captured with the SAME fixed bench, in the SAME project-local mode as pglite v3. Both measurements made on host darwin/M5 Max within ~10 min of each other; npx caches warm; identical corpus.

gate_decision.gate_target: warm-reopen steady-state metrics; RSS treated as informational only per baseline note about RSS measurement bug

root_cause_hypothesis: The 16-18% regression vs SQLite baseline is dominated by per-CLI-invocation agentdb registry initialization. Each `cli memory store` spawns a fresh node process which (under default config with neural.enabled=true) eagerly initializes the entire AgentDB ControllerRegistry: reasoningBank, hierarchicalMemory, learningSystem, explainableRecall, nightlyLearner, sonaTrajectory, etc. — even for memory_* axis CLI commands that only need the RVF storage path. Under Phase C-1, these controllers' bootstrap DDL (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE INDEX hnsw...) now runs against PostgresBackend, which is slower than the previous SQLite path (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector check + multiple per-controller HNSW idempotency probes). Verified by setting neural.enabled=false in .claude-flow/config.json — single store completes in 0.69s with no .swarm/memory.pglite/ created. Fix would require making the agentdb registry lazy (only init when an agentdb_* MCP tool is called), not gated on neural.enabled. This is an architectural change in the agentdb/memory router layer, not a substrate-level optimization.
recommended_phase_d_remediation: Make ControllerRegistry initialization lazy: gate it on actual agentdb_* tool invocation, not on every memory_* CLI call.
Or: shorten the per-controller DDL idempotency check — cache schema_version in a connection-cached lookup so CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS doesn't do catalog lookups on every CLI invocation.

Or: revisit gate threshold — the 10% band was set when pgvector was assumed performance-equivalent to SQLite; pgvector clusters have unavoidable per-connection init costs (CREATE EXTENSION, extension load) that SQLite doesn't pay. Documenting the realistic 15-20% steady-state regression as 'expected cost of MVCC + pgvector benefits' is a policy choice for the user, not the benchmark agent.
